How it works

  1. You set your priorities.Two starting points come from how 583 survey respondents ranked seven street conditions; people agreed only weakly (Kendall's W = 0.17 for women), so everyone can adjust.
  2. People report streets anonymously.Each phone gets 10 blind-signed tokens a day. The server can check a token is valid but can't tell which phone it came from.
  3. Reports become comfort scores.Once a week the server publishes each street's count of separate half-hours with reports, and what they were about, with random noise added (differential privacy, ε = 3 per report). Reports in the same half-hour count once. A street is flagged when its count reaches 4, about 5 separate half-hours, and older weeks fade by half every 14 days.
  4. Routes avoid uncomfortable streets within your limit.Using an established penalty method rather than a new algorithm, the app searches for the route with the least reported discomfort, and never picks one more than 15% longer than the shortest.
Test the defences

Try to fake-flag a clean street, a main road, the way a prankster or a coordinated group might.
